summary: Aomori Airport (AOJ/RJSA) is the main gateway to Aomori Prefecture in northern Honshu, located about 11 km south of central Aomori City. It has served the region since the 1960s and primarily handles domestic flights to major Japanese cities, with seasonal international charters. The airport sits near the Hakkoda Mountains and provides access to Hirosaki, Lake Towada, and the Shirakami-Sanchi World Heritage Site.
faqs:
Q: What airlines and destinations serve Aomori Airport?
A: Domestic flights are mainly operated by JAL and ANA to Tokyo Haneda, Osaka, Nagoya, and Sapporo; seasonal international charters may also operate. Check with airlines for current schedules.

Q: How far is Aomori Airport from Aomori Station?
A: It is about 11 km south of central Aomori. The airport limousine bus takes roughly 35–45 minutes to Aomori Station and about 50–60 minutes to Shin-Aomori Station, depending on traffic and weather.

Q: Is there public transportation from the airport?
A: Yes, scheduled airport buses connect the terminal to Aomori Station, Shin-Aomori Station, and other parts of Aomori Prefecture. Taxis and rental car counters are also available.

Q: Does Aomori Airport have international flights?
A: It primarily handles domestic flights, but seasonal or charter international services to destinations such as Seoul and Taipei have operated in the past. Check with airlines for current options.
transport_tips: The most convenient option is the airport limousine bus to Aomori Station and Shin-Aomori Station; buy tickets at the vending machine or counter in the arrival hall. Taxis are available but expensive for the 30–40 minute ride to central Aomori. If driving, rental car offices are near the terminal, and winter tires are essential from November to March.
local_tip: On clear days, the airport observation deck offers views of the Hakkoda Mountains; before security, pick up Aomori apple juice or cider—Aomori produces most of Japan's apples—as a last-minute local souvenir.
